# Starting and finding sessions

<!-- Generated by scripts/api_docs.py from the code and docs/api/groups.toml. Do not edit. -->

What a frontend does before it has a client: start or reopen a session, list the others, export one.

Names: `ForkedFrom`, `PickSession`, `SessionFlags`, `SessionInfo`, `Started`, `SystemText`, `UnknownSession`, `cli.extension_flags`, `cli.main`, `cli.session_flags`, `find_session`, `first_cursor`, `first_cursor_node`, `list_sessions`, `rename_session`, `start_session`, `to_markdown`

## ForkedFrom

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ForkedFrom
    session: str
    node: int
```

Where a forked session's walk was copied from: the source's `session` id and the `node` of
its tree the copy ends at.

## PickSession

```python
PickSession = Callable[[Sequence[SessionInfo], Sequence[SessionInfo]], SessionInfo]
```

What `-r` asks of a frontend: given the rows of the working directory and all rows (newest
first), the one to open.

## SessionFlags

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SessionFlags
    directory: Path | None = None
    continue_last: bool = False
    resume: bool = False
    session: str | None = None
    fork: str | None = None
    no_session: bool = False
    name: str | None = None
    system_prompt: str | None = None
    append_system_prompt: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    no_context_files: bool = False
```

What the session flags say, as `tau.cli.session_flags` parses them: `directory`
(`--session-dir`), `continue_last` (`-c`), `resume` (`-r`), `session` and `fork` (REFs),
`no_session` and `name` (`-n`), and the prompt flags (D20): `system_prompt`
(`--system-prompt`), `append_system_prompt` (`--append-system-prompt`, in order) and
`no_context_files` (`-nc`). A name (`-n`) is stripped and cannot be empty or hold a `/` or a
`:`. At most one of the first five choices; `no_session` takes none of
the others; a session that already has its prompt (`-c`, `-r`, `--session`, `--fork`) takes
neither `--system-prompt` nor `--append-system-prompt`. `ConfigError` otherwise.

### SessionFlags.of

```python
@classmethod
def of(cls, args: object, cwd: Path) -> 'SessionFlags'
```

The flags `session_flags()` parsed into `args`, with `--session-dir` and a path REF
made absolute against `cwd`, the directory they were typed in.

## SessionInfo

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SessionInfo
    id: str
    path: Path
    cwd: str | None
    name: str | None
    forked_from: ForkedFrom | None
    updated: float | None
    first: str | None
    error: str | None
```

One row of the catalog. `id` and `path` locate the session; `cwd` is its working
directory, `name` its name, `forked_from` its source; `updated` is the log's modification
time in seconds since the epoch (every synced write moves it); `first` is the text of its
first `User` node, read only when it has no `name` and only when asked for. A row that is not
a readable session has an `error` saying why, and no other field can be relied on.

### SessionInfo.title

```python
property title: str
```

What a frontend shows for it: the name, else the first message, on one line (cut to
80 characters), else `(no messages)`.

## Started

```python
@dataclass
class Started
    session: Session
    driver: Driver
    providers: Mapping[str, Provider]
    loaded: LoadedConfig
    model: str
    cwd: Path
    directory: Path | None
    created: bool
```

A running session: its `session` and `driver` (started), the `providers` the program
closes through `stop`, the `loaded` config and the `model` (selected for a new session, else
the one recorded at the first cursor), the session's working directory `cwd` (the process is
in it), the session's `directory` (`None`: in memory) and whether this run `created` it (a new
session or a fork). A session named during the run counts as used.

### Started.never_used

```python
property never_used: bool
```

This run created the session and it still has only the nodes it was created with, no
pending item and the name it was created with.

### Started.stop

```python
async def stop(self) -> None
```

Stop the driver; delete the session's directory if it was never used (while the lease
is still held); release the lease; close the providers.

## SystemText

```python
SystemText = Callable[[Path, LoadedConfig], str]
```

What a new session's `System` node says: given the session's working directory and the loaded
config. Called once, for a new session only.

## UnknownSession

```python
class UnknownSession(LookupError)
```

A ref that names no session, or a name or id prefix that names several. The message lists
the candidates with their `cwd` and age.

## tau.cli.extension_flags

```python
def extension_flags() -> argparse.ArgumentParser
```

A parser (`add_help=False`, for `parents=`) with the flags that choose extensions:
`-e VALUE` (repeatable; a path, or the key of a source: a discovered one or a built-in) and
`--no-extensions`.
`tau.start_session` reads them from the parsed args.

## tau.cli.main

```python
def main(
    argv: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    *,
    stdin: TextIO | None = None,
    stdout: TextIO | None = None,
    stderr: TextIO | None = None,
    environ: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,

```

Run `tau` with `argv` (default `sys.argv[1:]`); the other arguments default to
the process's streams, environment, and working directory. Returns the exit status.

## tau.cli.session_flags

```python
def session_flags() -> argparse.ArgumentParser
```

A parser (`add_help=False`, for `parents=`) with the flags that choose the session
(D18 section 5): `-c/--continue`, `-r/--resume`, `--session REF`, `--fork REF` and
`--no-session` (at most one), `-n/--name NAME` and `--session-dir DIR`; and the prompt flags
of a new session (D20): `--system-prompt TEXT`, `--append-system-prompt TEXT` (repeatable) and
`-nc/--no-context-files`. Pass the parsed arguments to `start_session`, which makes paths
absolute and rejects combinations.

## find_session

```python
def find_session(sessions: Path, session: str, *, first: bool = False) -> SessionInfo
```

The session `session` names, tried in this order: a path (it contains `/`), an id, an
exact name, a unique id prefix. The whole of `sessions` is searched. A name or prefix of
several sessions, or of none, is `UnknownSession`. With `first`, the row also has `first`.

## first_cursor

```python
async def first_cursor(session: Session, client: 'Client') -> int
```

The cursor a frontend shows, or `-p` sends to: the open cursor with the lowest id; if none
is open, the closed cursor with the lowest id, which `client` reopens (a new id with the old
labels). The choice among other cursors is the frontend's (D16, D17).

## first_cursor_node

```python
def first_cursor_node(session: Session) -> int
```

The node a frontend would show, without writing: the open cursor with the lowest id's
`at`, else the closed cursor with the lowest id's last node. What a fork or an export of a
session with no node given copies. `LookupError` for a session with no cursor.

## list_sessions

```python
def list_sessions(sessions: Path, *, cwd: Path | None = None) -> list[SessionInfo]
```

The rows of `sessions`, newest `updated` first; those whose `cwd` equals `cwd` (resolved)
exactly, or all with `cwd=None`. A directory that is not a readable session is a row with an
`error` and is listed either way. Reads `info.json` and stats `log` per session, and the
start of the log of a session with no name (its `first`). Anything that is not a directory is
ignored.

## rename_session

```python
def rename_session(path: Path, name: str) -> None
```

Give the session in `path` the name `name` (stripped); an empty `name` removes it. No lease
is taken: the file is replaced whole, and the last of two renames wins. `ConfigError` for a
name with a `/` or a `:` in it (a ref could not name the session by it), `ValueError` if
`info.json` is not readable.

## start_session

```python
async def start_session(
    args: object,
    *,
    environ: Mapping[str, str],
    cwd: Path,
    system: SystemText | None = None,
    prompts: Prompts | None = None,
    pick_session: PickSession | None = None,
    own: Sequence[Extension] = (),
    model: str | None = None,
    clock: Clock | None = None,
) -> Started
```

Start the session `args` (the parsed `session_flags()` and `extension_flags()`) choose, for
a program started in `cwd` with `environ`, as the module says. `own` are the program's own
extensions, ahead of the loaded ones; `model` is `--model`; `prompts` ask a person to trust a
project or to pick a model; `pick_session` is what `-r` asks; `system` is the text of a new
session's `System` node (default: D20's `tau.system_prompt`, from the prompt flags in `args`).

Raises what the steps raise: `ConfigError`, `TrustError`, `ExtensionLoadError`,
`UnknownSession`, `Leased`, `FileNotFoundError` for a session whose working directory is
gone. Nothing is created when a step before the session's fails, and a session this call
created is removed if a later step fails.

## to_markdown

```python
def to_markdown(
    nodes: Iterable[Node],
    *,
    thinking: bool = False,
    of: SessionInfo | None = None,
) -> str
```

`nodes` (a walk, root first) as Markdown. With `of`, the session's row, the document
starts with the header `tau export` writes: the title, `of`'s id and `cwd`, the node exported
(the walk's last) and `forked_from`. `LookupError` for a `Results` node whose call no earlier
`Assistant` node in `nodes` made.
